quote.text: A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.
quote.author: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748)

stories.headline: The Strikes Resume, Iran Answers Across Three Borders, and a Wedding Becomes the Number the War Turns On
stories.dek: After a month of relative quiet the United States struck about a hundred Revolutionary Guard targets around the Strait of Hormuz; Iran fired back at bases in Jordan and Kuwait and sent drones at Bahrain, hitting no Americans. The disputed toll is a house in Sirik, where Tehran says a strike killed a wedding party.

stories.headline: Nvidia Buys the Field Its Rivals Play On
stories.dek: The chipmaker signed for Hugging Face at about thirteen billion dollars — the open-model hub that eighteen million developers, and every rival's silicon, quietly depend on. Jensen Huang promises to keep it open and hardware-neutral. The question is whether the field's owner can stay neutral.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent · Indonesia
stories.headline: "Rojali": The Crowd That Never Buys
stories.dek: Indonesia's malls have never been busier or their tills quieter, and Indonesians have turned the gap into slang — a self-mocking meme that doubles as a hard economic indicator. Read closely, it is the visible edge of a consuming middle class that has been shrinking for five straight years, and of a growth dream with a hole in its foundation.

stories.headline: An Eleven-Year Gap Closes in Bangkok, and the Deliverable Is Rice
stories.dek: Wong and Anutin held the first Singapore–Thailand leaders' retreat since 2015, agreeing to negotiate four new pacts and to coordinate their back-to-back ASEAN chairs. The one signed thing worth its weight: a hundred thousand tonnes of Thai rice over five years.

stories.headline: Fine Paper, From the Fibre Up — and Why Thickness Is the Wrong Thing to Buy
stories.dek: The category everyone judges by weight is actually decided by sizing: the invisible coating that makes ink sit on a sheet instead of soaking in. Learn four variables and you can read any pad blind — and see exactly where the price stops buying performance and starts buying a name.

stories.headline: The Labs Shipped Trillion-Parameter Models This Month; the One That Fits Your Card Did Not Change
The Glasses Whose Whole Pitch Is What They Left Out
stories.dek: The reviews landed and the RayNeo iO goes on sale today at $479 — a monochrome heads-up display with no camera and no speaker, weighing thirty-three grams. Reviewers like the restraint; they are cooler on the beta software. Alongside it, Garmin's first titanium fēnix asks a four-figure question.

stories.headline: Geneva's Indies Steal the Week
stories.dek: Geneva Watch Days brought a record seventy-one brands to the lake, and the talking pieces came from the small houses: an MB&F wandering-hour under three thousand francs, and a Ming worldtimer that quietly fixes daylight saving. Plus a Sonos reset that asks to be believed twice.

stories.headline: Boyle Opens Venice With the Making of a Tabloid; the Lion Waits
stories.dek: Danny Boyle's "Ink" — Rupert Murdoch's 1969 relaunch of The Sun, adapted by James Graham — drew an ovation on the Lido, where the Golden Lion is still unawarded this weekend. On the charts, a K-pop octet takes a first American number one from a girl group that held it a week.

stories.headline: It's the Compulsion, Not the Hours — and the Arrow May Point Both Ways
stories.dek: A 2026 study of more than a thousand secondary-school students finds that anxiety tracks with problematic phone use, not screen time as such — and that anxious, bullied children are drawn toward compulsive use, not only harmed by it. For a parent at the Secondary One gate, that changes what to watch.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Portfolio Lens
stories.headline: A War Premium, High Real Yields, and a Market Holding Its Breath for the Payroll
stories.dek: One force runs the week: real yields, with a Middle-East war premium bolted on. It keeps the dollar firm and equities flat, puts a floor under gold even inside a down year, and leaves bitcoin caught between tight liquidity and a haven bid — while everyone waits on Friday's jobs print and a Fed that is debating a hike, not a cut.

stories.headline: Birding: The Free App That Recruited a Nation, and the Glass It Sent Them Chasing
stories.dek: Not staring at pigeons — a cumulative, quietly competitive hunt to find and identify wild birds by sight and sound, and to log every one. A ninety-six-million-strong world with a billion-observation database, a phone app that names birdsong in real time, and an optics arms race with no ceiling.

stories.headline: The Protein Powder That Did Nothing the Lifting Hadn't Already Done
stories.dek: A controlled trial in frail older adults added twenty grams of daily protein and dietary counselling to a supervised resistance-training programme — and got no extra strength, muscle or function for the trouble. The catch, and it matters: the ones who were under-eating protein to begin with did benefit.

stories.headline: The Padang's Biggest Bill Yet, and a Fukuoka Basho Worth the Flights
stories.dek: The Grand Prix stacks the Padang with headliners — a debut Singapore set from Lana Del Rey included — while a two-night stadium run and Japan's autumn sumo carry the marquees.
